facts.fact: tall, spare/gaunt figure
facts.quote: his tall, spare figure pass twice in a dark silhouette against the blind

facts.fact: hawk-like nose and thin frame, often curled up in his chair while thinking
facts.quote: his thin knees drawn up to his hawk-like nose

facts.fact: shares lodgings with Watson at Baker Street
facts.quote: remained in our lodgings in Baker Street, buried among his old books

facts.fact: unofficial consulting detective known across three continents
facts.quote: unofficial adviser and helper to everybody who is absolutely puzzled, throughout three continents

facts.fact: narrow but intense range of knowledge: violin-player, boxer, swordsman, lawyer, self-poisoner by cocaine and tobacco
facts.quote: violin-player, boxer, swordsman, lawyer, and self-poisoner by cocaine and tobacco

facts.fact: cold, precise, unemotional mind; considered the most perfect reasoning machine
facts.quote: the most perfect reasoning and observing machine that the world has seen

facts.fact: obsessive, tireless focus once absorbed in an unsolved problem, going days without rest
facts.quote: would go for days, and even for a week, without rest

facts.fact: indifferent to reward and royal favor, values a memento of intellect/character over wealth
facts.quote: turning away without observing the hand which the King had stretched out to him

facts.fact: master of disguise, unrecognizable even to Watson
facts.quote: I had to look three times before I was certain that it was indeed he

facts.fact: deduces a person's history from minute physical details (scuffed shoes, calluses, stains)
facts.quote: the leather is scored by six almost parallel cuts

facts.fact: examines crime scenes on hands and knees with a magnifying lens
facts.quote: fell upon his knees upon the floor and, with the lantern and a magnifying lens, began to examine minutely the cracks

facts.fact: plays the violin to relax or think through a case
facts.quote: hand me over my violin and let us try to forget for half an hour

facts.fact: visibly transforms when hot on a scent: darkened face, hard-set brows, animal intensity
facts.quote: His brows were drawn into two hard black lines, while his eyes shone out from beneath them with a steely glitter.

facts.fact: insists on data before forming theories
facts.quote: It is a capital mistake to theorise before one has data.

facts.fact: draws the line between passively seeing and actively observing
facts.quote: You see, but you do not observe. The distinction is clear.

facts.fact: depends on Watson as chronicler and companion, calling him 'my Boswell'
facts.quote: I am lost without my Boswell.

facts.fact: values Watson's quiet, undemanding companionship above conversation
facts.quote: You have a grand gift of silence, Watson

facts.fact: retains a lasting, singular regard for Irene Adler, always referring to her as 'the woman'
facts.quote: it is always under the honourable title of _the_ woman

antiFacts.why: the deerstalker never appears in the text; it originates from Sidney Paget's illustrations, not Conan Doyle's prose
never mentioned; his pipes in the text are a black clay pipe and an old briar pipe, not a calabash
the phrase never occurs in the text; 'elementary' appears once, describing a clue as 'rather elementary,' not addressed to Watson
explicitly denied: 'It was not that he felt any emotion akin to love for Irene Adler'; his regard is intellectual admiration, not romance

antiFacts.claim: warmly deferential toward Scotland Yard detectives
antiFacts.why: contradicted; he routinely solves cases 'abandoned as hopeless by the official police' and treats detectives like Lestrade with mild condescension

facts.fact: gained noticeable weight (about seven pounds) after his marriage, per Holmes's deduction
facts.quote: I think, Watson, that you have put on seven and a half pounds since I saw you.

facts.fact: former army doctor, carries a jezail bullet wound from his Afghan campaign
facts.quote: the jezail bullet which I had brought back in one of my limbs as a relic of my Afghan campaign

facts.fact: returns to civil medical practice and his own house in Kensington after marrying
facts.quote: As I drove home to my house in Kensington

facts.fact: shared rooms with Holmes at Baker Street before his own marriage
facts.quote: It was a few weeks before my own marriage, during the days when I was still sharing rooms with Holmes in Baker Street

facts.fact: self-deprecating about his own powers of observation next to Holmes's
facts.quote: I was always oppressed with a sense of my own stupidity in my dealings with Sherlock Holmes

facts.fact: practical and ready for sudden travel/adventure, a habit from his army days
facts.quote: My experience of camp life in Afghanistan had at least had the effect of making me a prompt and ready traveller.

facts.fact: writes up and publishes Holmes's cases, admittedly embellishing them
facts.quote: the enthusiasm which has prompted you to chronicle

facts.fact: carries an army revolver into danger at Holmes's request and stands watch armed
facts.quote: there may be some little danger, so kindly put your army revolver in your pocket

facts.fact: accompanies Holmes on dangerous stakeouts, weapon at the ready
facts.quote: I placed my revolver, cocked, upon the top of the wooden case behind which I crouched.

facts.fact: reacts to Holmes's deductions with exclamations of astonishment
facts.quote: My dear Holmes,” said I, “this is too much.

facts.fact: introduced by Holmes as his 'intimate friend and associate' whom clients can trust completely
facts.quote: This is my intimate friend and associate, Dr. Watson, before whom you can speak as freely as before myself.

facts.fact: married, but still returns to stay at Baker Street with Holmes when his wife is away
facts.quote: My wife was on a visit to her mother’s, and for a few days I was a dweller once more in my old quarters at Baker Street.

antiFacts.claim: physically stout or heavyset in build
antiFacts.why: no build is described beyond the seven-pound weight gain since marriage; a stout/heavyset build is never stated
contradicted; Holmes deduces he is 'an active member of the medical profession' from professional signs (iodoform smell, nitrate stains) and he maintains a real Kensington practice

antiFacts.claim: skeptical of or resistant to Holmes's methods
antiFacts.why: contradicted; he is an admiring, willing companion who calls himself dense by comparison and enthusiastically chronicles Holmes's cases
never mentioned; only his wife appears, with no reference to any children

antiFacts.claim: wears a bowler hat and carries a cane as a signature look
antiFacts.why: invented visual shorthand from illustrations/adaptations; no such signature appearance is described in the text
